Per frozen spec this is an environment limitation, disclosed as exploratory-bound, NOT a measurement failure and NOT a scientific negative.

Learned confidence is model-derived softmax over learned candidate logits (plus learned rewrite logit when rewriting) with a learned inverse temperature, gated UNKNOWN<0.80; for no-candidate tasks (no-applicable/empty) confidence uses a structural abstain constant 0.05+hash-jitter mirroring the RULE proxy - disclosed in metrics.learned.confidence_definition; the no-candidate strata therefore contribute partially structural, not fully model-derived, confidence to ECE.
ECE bootstrap CI (2000 resamples) is reported for RULE only; the learned overall ECE 0.0518 is a point estimate on n=70 without resampled CI.

First full run of this script produced LEARNED 0/40 with near-constant confidence and decreasing reward caused by a GRPO gradient bug (whole-group log-prob scalar x mean-centered advantage vector ~ zero gradient). The bug was fixed (per-member log-prob vector) and the run re-executed; the buggy run's numbers are not part of this evidence base.

Train window of 21 orthogonal standard tasks is leak-free vs 9 held-out and 10 mixed evaluation forms (asserts in run; train_split_inventory.json); binomial/McNemar tests are computed on the deterministic frozen task fixture (n=40 pooled / 30 orthogonal).
Synthetic alias-OOD generalization evidence does not imply organic real-web alias formation; pooled+heldout+mixed results are confined to the frozen task-graph DGP.
Confidence calibration (ECE learned 0.052 vs RULE 0.080) is measured on the full 70-task held-out evaluation, not the training distribution.
Economics counters measure in-process synthetic latency and op counts; they do not include browser/network work (live stage unavailable).
